newsitem.title: GREECE: ATTICA ENTEPR SEES 96 NET INCOME UP 31PCT.
newsitem.headline: ATTICA ENTEPR SEES 96 NET INCOME UP 31PCT.

text.p: Greek shipper Attica Enterprises expects its 1996 after-tax profits to exceed 4.0 billion drachmas, up more than 30.5 percent on 1995, its marketing director Yannis Criticos told Reuters.
"We estimate that after-tax profits will exceed 4.0 billion drachmas in 1996 against 3.063 billion in 1995, an increase of more than 30.5 percent," said Criticos.
Turnover is expected to be greater than 13.5 billion drachmas in 1996 against 9.085 billion in 1995, an increase of more than 48.8 percent, he said.
"These estimates exceed by far our 1995 prospectus forecasts, he said.

Criticos cautioned against drawing conclusions by just comparing figures between 1995 and 1996 without taking into account that Attica's two Superfast I and II ferries were in operation for the entire year in 1996 compared to seven and a half months in 1995.
The firm's Superfast I vessel started operations on April 15, 1995 and Superfast Ii followed on June 16.
Criticos added that the payback period on that investment was less than two years and a half.
"Return on equity is expected to rise by more than 40 percent in 1996. It rose by more than 30 percent in 1995," he said.
Attica Enterprises has two new vessels, Superfast III and IV, under construction at Kvaerner mass Yards in Finland and expects delivery in 1998.
The investment is financed by loans from Chase Manhattan Bank and the Finnish export financing organisation representing 80 percent of the investment outlay and the rest from retained earnings.
Attica Enterprises is participating in the Athens general share index and the IFC emerging markets share index. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
